results.evidence: Unsalted SHA-256 reveals move 2 in 3 guesses. The same guesses with an unknown 256-bit salt produce no match.
Known PRNG seed predicts r=…4099b181 and reveals move 2. Predicting that r does not open a CSPRNG commitment.

Known x=7 lets one point open as rock (r=11) or scissors (r'=49625181090152678041156048692603245798570123667486754432466682454743648019026). The same forged opening fails against the pinned generator.
results.limitation: No experiment can prove an unknown discrete logarithm; the pinned hash-to-curve construction provides the binding assumption.

results.evidence: A naive referee trusts a changed move. Pedersen opening verification rejects paper against a rock commitment.
An unguarded match accepts the copied point. The referee rejects duplicates, and the signature payload changes with player ID.
Early exit inspects 1 versus 64 characters. Fixed-work comparison inspects 64 in both cases.
results.limitation: Operation counts demonstrate the branch difference; they do not establish a remotely exploitable timing leak.

results.evidence: A length-only validator accepts a 33-byte identity-like encoding; strict compressed-point parsing rejects it.
A reveal arriving one millisecond after the deadline is accepted without a timer and rejected by the referee deadline rule. The API test checks actual forfeit behavior.
A signature over C alone verifies again in another round. A signature over tournament, match, round, player, mode, and C fails when round changes.
A plain log displays an altered winner. The browser verifier detects the changed event hash and broken chain.
results.limitation: An operator could rewrite the entire chain without an external checkpoint.
